headline: Mexico's Home Health Program Reaches Nearly 11 Million in One Year
meta_description: Mexico's home health initiative delivered 22.8 million consultations to vulnerable populations through thousands of health workers.
summary_short: Mexico's home health program made over 22 million visits to older adults and people with disabilities in a single year.
body:
Mexico's home health program delivered 22.8 million consultations to 10.9 million older adults and people with disabilities in just one year—a massive undertaking that brought essential care directly to vulnerable populations.

The scale of this effort becomes clear in the workforce behind it: 21,267 health workers carried out home visits across the country, each one representing a direct connection between the health system and people who might otherwise struggle to access care. This distributed model bypasses barriers of mobility and geography that often prevent vulnerable populations from receiving timely medical attention.

The program reveals an important shift in how nations can approach healthcare for their most dependent citizens. Rather than requiring older adults and people with disabilities to travel to clinics, the system brings trained professionals to their homes—a model that reduces strain on both patients and overcrowded facilities.
